thread:
maya: quick check — UX ask: add a small "preview rollback" button on the rollout card so operators can see what a fallback would look like before committing?

sam: 👍 love the idea. is this just a read-only diff or do we simulate traffic?

maya: start with read-only diff of policy + sampled example traces. later add dry-run with live traffic sampling.

devin: important: must show which requests would be affected (by routing key, quota class, error type). otherwise operators get false confidence.

nora: agree. also show audit id and RCA links for the triggering events so they can trace back.

maya: proposed preview contents: (1) policy delta diff, (2) sample N=50 requests that would route to fallback, (3) error triggers matched, (4) telemetry delta estimate (qps/latency/cost).

liam: for sample requests we only have hashed keys and anonymized tokens. don't leak prompt text. ops-bot: reminder: PII rule — samples must be sanitized.

maya: yes — sanitize, but include metadata like route, region, model variant, and approximate token counts.

sam: UX question: where to surface the button? on rollout timeline next to "apply" or inside the policy editor?

nora: put it on the timeline so you test the exact commit state. editor preview could be another affordance.

devin: behavioral heuristics: if the preview shows >X% of traffic affected or >Y cost delta, show a warning banner. what thresholds?

liam: ops should be able to configure thresholds per org. sensible defaults: X=5% traffic, Y=10% cost increase.

maya: also need a safe-mode toggle: "simulate only for me" vs "simulate against sampled production traffic (sanitized)" so early checks don't affect others.

sam: floating idea: allow an operator to run the preview and get a temporary telemetry snapshot ID that is stored in audit logs. then if rollback happens later we can link snapshot -> decision.

nora: love that. auditability is key. include who ran preview, when, what sampling params. store as event in rollout timeline.

devin: implementation note: sampling for dry-run can be expensive. we should reuse streaming traces and cached KV for prefix matches to estimate without full re-execution.

liam: +1. we can run a fast rule-evaluator against recent request headers to classify affected set. no model execution required for preview.

maya: UI microcopy: button label options: "Preview rollback impact", "Simulate fallback", "Preview fallback". which is clearest?

sam: "Preview fallback impact" is explicit. keep it long but clear.

nora: add tiny tooltip: "Shows which requests would be routed to fallback and estimated telemetry impact. Does not change live traffic."

devin: edgecases: what if current rollout already has partial fallbacks (canary)? preview needs to show combined effect.

maya: noted. preview must compute delta from current live state to post-rollback state and show both baseline and after numbers.

liam: ops-bot: deploy-check: is there any security review needed for storing sanitized samples in the audit timeline?

ops-bot: automated response: create a ticket to security with sample retention TTL and sanitization plan. include encryption-at-rest and access controls.

maya: final asks for eng: (a) backend API endpoint preview/estimate (returns diff + sample ids), (b) telemetry estimator that can compute cost/latency delta, (c) timeline event model to persist preview runs, (d) UI small modal with samples and diff.

sam: I'll take (d) and (a) sketch. devin you take (b) and liam (c) + security ticket?

devin: yep, will prototype estimator using prefix match + cached latency histograms.

liam: will open security ticket after we have sample schema. also will add org-level thresholds to settings.

nora: quick UX nit: when operator runs preview, show a subtle spinner + cancel button — previews can take a few seconds.

maya: thanks all. I'll draft a short mock and share in #eng-platform tomorrow. if anyone wants to pair on the prototype ping me. :sparkles:
